items.title: Headlines for November 10, 2026 | Democracy Now!
items.excerpt: ## GOP Rep. Thomas Massie Introduces Articles of Impeachment Against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth Nov 10, 2026 Republican Congressmember Thomas Massie introduced articles of impeachment against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth on Monday for “high crimes and misdemeanors.” The eight impeachment articles accuse Hegseth of violating the 1973 War Powers Resolution by continuing to attack Iran even after both chambers of Congress ordered the Trump administration to stop. He’s also accused of illegally waging war against Yemen, ignoring laws designed to reduce civilian casualties, overseeing “extrajudicial killings” in attacks on boats in the Caribbean Sea and eastern Pacific, abducting Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro without congressional authorization, and suppressing the free speech rights of Democratic Senator Mark Kelly in retaliation for reminding troops not to obey illegal orders. Congressmember Massie outlined the charges during a speech from the House floor. > Rep. Thomas Massie: “Wherefore, Secretary of Defense Peter Hegseth, by such conduct, has demonstrated that he will remain a threat to the Constitution if allowed to remain in office, and has acted in a manner grossly incompatible with his duties and the rule of law, Peter Brian Hegseth thus warrants impeachment and trial, removal from office and disqualification to hold and enjoy any office of honor, trust or profit under the United States.” It’s expected the House will vote on Hegseth’s impeachment on Wednesday. Only a few Republican defectors would be needed for a simple majority, setting up a Senate trial on whether to remove Hegseth. On Monday, President Trump said he would stand by Hegseth if he’s impeached. ## Pentagon Retreats from Second U.K. Base Due to Alleged Threat from Iran Nov 10, 2026 The Wall Street Journal reports the Pentagon has evacuated aircraft from a second base in the United Kingdom due to another alleged threat from Iran. U.S. refueling tankers were reportedly moved from a base in Mildenhall on Monday. Last month, the Pentagon pulled B-1 bombers out of another British base. Meanwhile, Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps says two more ships, including a supertanker, are on fire near the Strait of Hormuz after using what Iranian officials have called an “unauthorized route.” Iran has claimed 11 strikes on ships over a 10-day span. The continued attacks on shipping came as Iran’s Foreign Ministry said it could reopen the strait within 48 hours if the U.S. agrees to Tehran’s list of demands. > Esmail Baghaei: “If the U.S. meets the demands put forward by Iran, the situation in the region could see a positive shift in as little as two days, and security in the Strait of Hormuz could also be restored.” On Monday, President Trump spoke with Qatar’s prime minister, who’s acted as a mediator in efforts to end the war. After the talks, Trump claimed there was “positive momentum” in negotiations for a deal with Iran. > President Donald Trump: “The military action doesn’t seem to be a very necessary thing, but we’re locked and loaded, ready to go for any reason that changes. Israel and the entire Middle East are protected from Iranian danger and threats, and we’re seeing momentum toward the end of this conflict. I think it’s going to be ending fairly soon.” Since the U.S. and Israel launched the war on Iran in February, Trump has claimed more than 40 times that the war was close to an end, that a deal was near, or that the war was already over. ## Trump Raises New Election Conspiracy Theory After Democrats Sweep Midterms Nov 10, 2026 Democrats are continuing to build on their historic wins in last week’s midterm elections as votes continue to be counted. In Mississippi, Scott Colom’s lead over Republican incumbent Senator Cindy Hyde-Smith has topped 2,500 votes, with just two batches of ballots left to be counted before a Friday deadline to certify the results. In Colorado, Republican Congressmember Lauren Boebert is trailing in her bid to hold on to her seat. On Monday, CNN projected Boebert will lose the race to Democrat Eileen Laubacher, a retired U.S. Navy admiral who served on the National Security Council under President Joe Biden. On Monday, President Trump reversed his previous comment that he was “absolutely willing” to accept the results of the midterm elections. Trump wrote on his Truth Social platform, “Does anybody really believe that this 'Election' was honest. How could the Polls be so wrong???” ## Schumer Faces Pressure to Step Aside as Chris Van Hollen Hints at Run for Senate Majority Leader Senate Democrats could be headed for a leadership shakeup, after Maryland Senator Chris Van Hollen indicated Monday he’s open to running for Senate majority leader when the new Congress convenes in January. A source close to Van Hollen told Politico the Maryland Democrat is thinking about a run after he “received an outpouring of calls and is now in active listening mode. The door is not shut.” This comes as a growing number of Senate Democrats have called for new leadership or refused to commit to supporting New York Senator Chuck Schumer for majority leader. ... ## Senate Advances Bill to Speed Construction of Fossil Fuel Projects and Data Centers In more news from Capitol Hill, the Senate voted 73 to 25 Monday to take up a sweeping permitting reform bill. It was advanced by nearly every Republican and 22 Democrats. Environmental groups have called the legislation an “aggressive attack on federal environmental protections in order to facilitate rapid, unregulated development of fracked gas power plants, dirty fossil fuel pipelines, and expensive hyperscale data centers.” Meanwhile, Indigenous leaders, including New Mexico Governor-elect Deb Haaland, argue the bill would undermine tribal sovereignty. More than 160 health, consumer, religious and environmental groups are calling on Congress to instead pass the No AI Data Centers on Federal Lands Act. It’s sponsored by Michigan democratic socialist Congresswoman Rashida Tlaib, who said, “[The] elections send a clear message that Americans want their representatives to protect their health and environment, not sell them out to Big Tech and Big Oil.” ... ## African National Congress Suffers Its ... In South Africa, the African National Congress, the party of Nelson Mandela, suffered its worst results in local elections on Sunday. The ANC won just 31% of the vote, though it remains South Africa’s largest party. Its main rival, the Democratic Alliance, said it won the votes of more than 1 million Black South ⁠Africans for the first time.

items.title: Fed officials open door to a half-point hike after inflation beats expectations By Reuters
items.excerpt: WASHINGTON, Nov 10 (Reuters) - The odds that the Federal Reserve may raise interest rates by half a percentage point next month jumped on Tuesday after US data showed prices rising faster than expected in October and policymakers opened the door to a quicker pace of rate hikes. The Consumer Price Index rose 0.4% on a monthly basis in October, down from the 0.6% registered in September as energy inflation receded. The index excluding volatile food and energy prices, however, rose 0.3% for the third month in a row, evidence of persistent "core" inflation and price pressures spreading through the economy. In comments overnight in London, Fed Governor Christopher Waller said a core CPI reading of 0.3% in October would prompt him to consider a half-percentage-point hike at the US central bank’s December 8-9 meeting. With a quarter-percentage-point hike all but assured, market bets on a larger increase were rapidly building amid a powerful bond market selloff. The probability was close to 15% in the middle of the morning before retreating to about 10% in the late afternoon. If core consumer prices rise 0.3% or more from September, "a stronger policy move may be needed," Waller said at a conference hosted by King’s Business School and the Money Macro & Finance Society. "In that case, I believe a 50-basis-point hike in the policy rate should be considered at the December meeting." Sticking with a smaller rate increase, Waller said, risks hurting the Fed’s inflation-fighting credibility, given inflation that is too high and appears to be broadening. Economists polled by Reuters had expected core monthly inflation to drop to 0.2% in October. The CPI data and Waller’s comments drove the selling in the US Treasury market, with the yield on 2-year notes — a proxy for Fed policy expectations — rising by the most since early April 2025. Dallas Fed President Lorie Logan said in separate remarks at an energy conference that it "may be possible to move more rapidly" than the quarter-percentage-point hike approved in September. items.title: US consumer prices rise briskly for third straight month | Financial Newsletter
items.excerpt: Reuters November 10, 2026 1:40 PM By Lucia Mutikani WASHINGTON, Nov 10 (Reuters) – US consumer prices increased more than expected in October amid higher costs for food and accommodation, cementing expectations that ‌the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates next month. The Consumer Price Index report from the Labor Department on Tuesday also showed a strong buildup of underlying inflation pressures for a third straight month. It followed data last week showing the labor market regained momentum in October. Inflation is being driven by the US-Israeli war with Iran, which has boosted oil prices, the Trump administration’s import tariffs, resilient ‌consumer spending ⁠and aggressive business investment in ⁠artificial intelligence technology. The rising cost of ​living ⁠contributed to the heavy losses suffered by President Donald Trump’s Republican Party in the midterm elections last week. Fed Governor Christopher Waller said on Tuesday the US central bank should raise rates next month, adding that “a stronger policy move may be needed.” Waller also raised the prospect of an aggressive 50-basis-point hike. “The Fed seems to be falling behind the curve on inflation, and the October hold is looking like a policy mistake,” said Stephen Juneau, an economist at Bank of America Securities. “We see a rising risk that the Fed will have to hike again in January, rather than March.” The CPI increased 0.4% last month after advancing 0.6% in September, the department’s Bureau of Labor Statistics said. It was the third consecutive month of gains of 0.4% or more. Economists polled by Reuters had forecast the CPI would climb 0.3% over the month. The BLS did not publish year-over-year inflation readings because last year’s federal government shutdown prevented the collection of consumer price data in October 2025, leaving no comparison base. Some economists used the average index for September and November 2025 to estimate the year-over-year rate of change for the October CPI. Others used interpolated levels from independent sources. Their estimates for the October year-over-year CPI ranged from a gain of 3.9% to 4.0%. Annual consumer inflation was 3.7% in September. Shelter, which includes rents and hotel and motel rooms, accounted for more than 30% of the monthly increase in the CPI. Shelter costs rose 0.3% after climbing 0.4% in September. Food prices surged 0.5% after barely rising in the prior three months. Grocery store prices climbed 0.4%, boosted by a 0.9% jump in the cost of beef. Egg prices rose 0.6%, while fruits and vegetables were 0.6% more expensive. Prices for dairy products increased 0.6%. The cost of snacks surged 1.0%. Rising prices at the supermarket could be an early sign that high diesel prices are filtering through ​to consumers. The cost of eating out also increased last month, with prices of food away from home rising 0.5% after a 0.2% gain in ‌September. The cost ⁠of full-service meals jumped 0.7%. “This may finally be the beginning of a pass-through of higher transportation costs to grocery prices,” said Stephen Stanley, chief US economist at Santander US Capital Markets. “If this is indeed happening, it could be a feature across ‌a broad array of goods categories.” Gasoline prices climbed 1.0% after soaring 9.1% in September. Consumers also paid more for electricity. Although diesel prices have eased off all-time highs, they remain on an upward trend, rising 2.7% in October after increasing 11.9% in September. Consumers could get some relief at the pump, with oil prices down at least 10% so far this month, but the pressure is unlikely to ease elsewhere, economists warned. Inflation-adjusted average weekly earnings fell again in October. MORE ⁠RATE HIKES ANTICIPATED The so-called core CPI, which excludes volatile food and energy items, increased 0.3% in October for ‌the third straight month. The so-called core CPI was forecast to have climbed 0.2% in October. Economists estimated that year-over-year core CPI inflation gained 2.8% in October. Annual core CPI inflation rose 2.6% in September. Financial markets are pricing in a roughly 89% chance of a 25-basis-point rate hike next month, and ​expect another increase in March, CME Group’s FedWatch tool showed. The Fed left its benchmark overnight interest rate in the 3.75%-4.00% range last month. Economists said only a substantial selloff in equity markets or widening credit spreads would prevent the Fed from tightening monetary policy in December. ... US Treasury yields were ​mostly higher. Underlying inflation last month was driven by a 0.3% rise in ‌owners’ equivalent rent, a measure of the amount homeowners would pay to rent or earn from renting their property. Prices for hotel and motel rooms rose 0.6%. Airline fares increased 0.4%. The cost of recreation services climbed 0.9%, while that of motor vehicle insurance advanced 0.7%. Doctor visits and hospital services also cost more. But the price of health insurance dropped 1.8%. The BLS updated the data used to calculate this component. Overall services prices excluding energy increased 0.3% after rising 0.4% in September. Tariff effects were also evident in ​October. Prices of household furnishings and supplies rebounded 0.7% and the cost of toys increased 1.8%. There were more price gains for computers and peripherals, reflecting the AI spending boom. Prices for smartphones rose a record 1.4%. There were also increases in the prices of new vehicles and medication. But used car and truck prices dropped 1.2%. Core goods prices increased 0.2% after climbing 0.3% in September. The ‌missing data from last year have no impact on the calculation of the Personal Consumption Expenditures Price Index readings that the Fed tracks to gauge progress toward its inflation target. Based on last month’s data, economists estimated that core PCE inflation rose 0.4% after advancing 0.3% in September. In the 12 months through October, core PCE inflation is projected to have increased 3.3% after gaining 3.1% in the 12 months ‌through September. These estimates could be impacted by producer price data for October that is due to be released ⁠on Friday.

items.excerpt: November 10, 2026, 3:46 PM EST ... ## What to know today - HOUSE GOP LEADER: House Republicans elected Jim Jordan, R-Ohio, as their new leader to replace outgoing Speaker Mike Johnson, R-La., when the new Congress convenes in January. Jordan defeated Majority Leader Steve Scalise, R-La., a close Johnson ally, for the top spot. - SENATE GOP LEADER: Senate Republicans re-elected John Thune, R-S.D., as their party leader, despite a push from some conservatives to delay the vote. - IMPEACHMENT EFFORT: The House could vote tonight on Republican Rep. Thomas Massie's resolution to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth over the U.S. war with Iran. At a news conference this morning, Hegseth called the effort "a farce" and a "stunt" aimed at damaging President Donald Trump. ... ## Thune re-elected Senate GOP leader Senate Republicans have re-elected Sen. John Thune, R-S.D., as their leader for the next Congress. Thune, who has been serving as majority leader since 2025, will now lead a GOP minority in the chamber next year. Thune’s victory today comes even as some Senate Republicans called to delay leadership elections to discuss how the party would act in the face of major midterm losses. But ultimately no challenger emerged to Thune. Sen. items.title: Headlines for November 10, 2026 | Democracy Now!
items.excerpt: ## GOP Rep. Thomas Massie Introduces Articles of Impeachment Against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth Nov 10, 2026 Republican Congressmember Thomas Massie introduced articles of impeachment against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth on Monday for “high crimes and misdemeanors.” The eight impeachment articles accuse Hegseth of violating the 1973 War Powers Resolution by continuing to attack Iran even after both chambers of Congress ordered the Trump administration to stop. He’s also accused of illegally waging war against Yemen, ignoring laws designed to reduce civilian casualties, overseeing “extrajudicial killings” in attacks on boats in the Caribbean Sea and eastern Pacific, abducting Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro without congressional authorization, and suppressing the free speech rights of Democratic Senator Mark Kelly in retaliation for reminding troops not to obey illegal orders. Congressmember Massie outlined the charges during a speech from the House floor. ... It’s expected the House will vote on Hegseth’s impeachment on Wednesday. Only a few Republican defectors would be needed for a simple majority, setting up a Senate trial on whether to remove Hegseth. On Monday, President Trump said he would stand by Hegseth if he’s impeached. ... Democrats are continuing to build on their historic wins in last week’s midterm elections as votes continue to be counted. In Mississippi, Scott Colom’s lead over Republican incumbent Senator Cindy Hyde-Smith has topped 2,500 votes, with just two batches of ballots left to be counted before a Friday deadline to certify the results. In Colorado, Republican Congressmember Lauren Boebert is trailing in her bid to hold on to her seat. On Monday, CNN projected Boebert will lose the race to Democrat Eileen Laubacher, a retired U.S. Navy admiral who served on the National Security Council under President Joe Biden. On Monday, President Trump reversed his previous comment that he was “absolutely willing” to accept the results of the midterm elections. Trump wrote on his Truth Social platform, “Does anybody really believe that this 'Election' was honest. How could the Polls be so wrong???” ## Schumer Faces Pressure to Step Aside as Chris Van Hollen Hints at Run for Senate Majority Leader Senate Democrats could be headed for a leadership shakeup, after Maryland Senator Chris Van Hollen indicated Monday he’s open to running for Senate majority leader when the new Congress convenes in January. A source close to Van Hollen told Politico the Maryland Democrat is thinking about a run after he “received an outpouring of calls and is now in active listening mode. The door is not shut.” This comes as a growing number of Senate Democrats have called for new leadership or refused to commit to supporting New York Senator Chuck Schumer for majority leader. Joining the call is a major labor union, the International Association of Machinists and Aerospace Workers, which wrote in a letter to Schumer on Monday, “We believe this is the right moment for a new generation to lead Senate Democrats.” Meanwhile, Connecticut Democratic Senator Richard Blumenthal said he’s open to new leadership if a challenger to Schumer emerges. > Sen. Richard Blumenthal: “But we need to have a conversation about leadership going forward, because we need new energy and ideas.” ## Senate Advances Bill to Speed Construction of Fossil Fuel Projects and Data Centers In more news from Capitol Hill, the Senate voted 73 to 25 Monday to take up a sweeping permitting reform bill. It was advanced by nearly every Republican and 22 Democrats. Environmental groups have called the legislation an “aggressive attack on federal environmental protections in order to facilitate rapid, unregulated development of fracked gas power plants, dirty fossil fuel pipelines, and expensive hyperscale data centers.” Meanwhile, Indigenous leaders, including New Mexico Governor-elect Deb Haaland, argue the bill would undermine tribal sovereignty. More than 160 health, consumer, religious and environmental groups are calling on Congress to instead pass the No AI Data Centers on Federal Lands Act. It’s sponsored by Michigan democratic socialist Congresswoman Rashida Tlaib, who said, “[The] elections send a clear message that Americans want their representatives to protect their health and environment, not sell them out to Big Tech and Big Oil.”

items.excerpt: ## We Are Imaginary releases music video FILIPINO indie-rock band We Are Imaginary has dropped the official music video for “Are We There Yet?,” the latest single from their 2026 self-titled album. Directed by Jam Lasin of Cream Flower, the music video captures the band in their jamming element, stitching together performances, candid moments, and visual references that pay tribute to their 18-year career as an underground force in the Filipino independent music scene. The music video also traces the highs and lows of band life. The track, which retains the post-punk guitar sensibilities of its original demo, is available on all streaming platforms. ## 2 Valid IDs hits P100-million box office milestone POWERED by word of mouth and a growing audience campaign, the small independent film 2 Valid IDs starring Marietta Subong (a.k.a. Pokwang) and directed by Ma-an L. Asuncion-Dagñalan, has crossed the P100-million mark at the Philippine box office. It has become one of the highest-grossing films in Cinemalaya history. Now on its fourth week in cinemas, the film generated interest online for its relatable storyline. Written by Abet Pagdadaganan Raz, 2 Valid IDs follows Sylvia, a poor provincial farmer trying to secure financial assistance for her hospitalized husband, made difficult due to frustrating bureaucratic processes that require two valid government-issued IDs. At Cinemalaya 2026, it won three awards: Best Actress for Ms. Subong, the Special Jury Award, and the Audience Choice Award. ## The Lord of the Rings concert coming in 2027 FILM Concerts Philippines has revealed that they will be presenting The Lord of the Rings: The Fellowship of the Ring in Concert on March 4, 5, and 6, 2027, at The Theatre at Solaire, Parañaque City. As Peter Jackson’s acclaimed film plays on the big screen, Howard Shore’s Academy Award-winning score will be performed live by the 247-member ensemble of the Filharmonika Orchestra, the Philippine Madrigal Singers’ adult and boys’ choirs, and soloist Malena Rampi, under the baton of conductor Reuben Blundell. This will mark the largest ensemble Film Concerts Philippines has assembled to date. Since the film’s premiere in 2008, The Fellowship of the Ring in Concert has been performed by leading orchestras worldwide. Exclusive pre-sale access for Film Concerts Philippines community members is ongoing until Nov. 11, with public ticket sales beginning Nov. 20. ## Zoë Kravitz, John C. Reilly star in How to Rob a Bank THE upcoming film How to Rob a Bank kicks off with a gang of masked livestreaming bank robbers turning the FBI on its head. In the middle of the investigation is special agent John West, played by John C. Reilly, who forms an unlikely partnership with a software engineer on house arrest, played by Zoë Kravitz. Their combined skills are needed to take the viral criminals down. How to Rob A Bank also stars Nicholas Hoult, Anna Sawai, Rhenzy Feliz, Christian Slater, and Pete Davidson. The film arrives in Philippine cinemas on Nov. 11. ## LEYO releases new EP FILIPINO singer-songwriter LEYO has reimagined the Filipino harana (serenade) with modern sensibilities in Akda sa Pag-alala, a six-track EP released under Sony Music Entertainment. Blending classic OPM, acoustic pop, and R&B, it is a personal collection shaped by affection, longing, vulnerability, and self-discovery. It balances guitar riffs and bass lines with jazzy, bossa nova-lite inflections, borrowing from a range of influences like The Beatles, Stevie Wonder, the APO Hiking Society, and the Manila Sound. The EP’s producers include 2026 Awit Awards winner Brian Lotho, Rain Santana, and LEYO himself. Akda sa Pag-alala is out now on all digital music platforms worldwide. ## George Michael concert film coming in Nov. GEORGE MICHAEL Entertainment, in partnership with Mercury Studios, has announced the start of the worldwide theatrical release of a brand-new, never-before-seen film titled George Michael: The Faith Tour, with screenings beginning on Nov. 11. Shot at the iconic Palais Omnisports de Paris-Bercy during the European leg of the Faith Tour in 1988, the film captures a turning point that transformed George Michael from a global superstar into an era-defining artist. Directed by Andy Morahan and David Austin, this once-lost film has been restored and remastered, transforming archival footage assembled from a 14-camera shoot captured on 35mm film into a cinematic experience. ... ## Dune, Dune: Part Two return for a limited time TO RELIVE the journey before experiencing the third and final installment of the film series this December, Dune and Dune: Part Two will be back in cinemas and IMAX for one week starting Nov. 11. The screenings will include an exclusive sneak peek of Dune: Part Three, the conclusion to Denis Villeneuve’s Dune trilogy. The film stars Timothée Chalamet, Zendaya, Jason Momoa, Javier Bardem, Rebecca Ferguson, Florence Pugh, Robert Pattinson, and Anya Taylor-Joy, among others. It opens in cinemas and IMAX on Dec. 16, with more sneak previews slated for Dec. 15.
